The membership plot repeats author labels inside marks as well as on the axis; a dot or matrix encoding could reduce repetition. These are styling limitations, not additional pass/fail grades.

limitations: Small correlated pilot: source graph samples contain only 4–8 vertices; cases and conversational variants are not independent production requests.
Source lineages and exact graph contents are separated across splits, while some question wording is shared. This measures source/graph transfer, not broad language generalization.
Stage evaluation uses fixed preceding context. Complete workflow success is reported separately.
Automatic numeric/citation, schema, field, data-binding and rendering checks do not prove every interpretation or chart conveys the right meaning. No human preference labels were collected.
The error-recovery workflow deliberately injects an invalid first draft; it is not a naturally occurring student failure.
Comparison is base versus two specialized adapters. A jointly trained single adapter was not evaluated.
An unrelated GPU workload was observed during evaluation. Reported elapsed times include generation, validation and resource contention; they are not isolated speed benchmarks.
Only one completed run per input and configuration is reported; repeated-run stability has not been measured.
One supervised epoch and the selected rank/learning rate were not established as optimal. Training uses NF4; actual measured serving uses the FP8 checkpoint.
Earlier runs with insufficient context, unmatched adapter names, decoder defects, or native GPU resource exhaustion remain diagnostic and are excluded from these primary comparisons.
Shared GPU0 leaves about11GiB idle headroom with this model profile. The bounded gMatch pools do not cap every backend allocation; larger graphs need separate capacity testing.
Clearer chart validation feedback did not make the focused development repair pass. Chart reliability is reported from the frozen probes rather than assumed from the new feedback.
